questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the structural brain abnormalities in schizophrenia is incorrect?

options.text: There is a significant reduction in brain volume of the cerebral hemispheres, cerebral cortex and central grey matter.
Ventricular enlargement has been found in post-mortem studies.
Hippocampal formation was noted to be significantly smaller in the right and the left hemispheres.
The reduction in hippocampal volume in male schizophrenics was smaller than that in female schizophrenics.
Changes have been observed in the entorhinal cortex, which are indicative of disturbed development.

correct_answer.text: The reduction in hippocampal volume in male schizophrenics was smaller than that in female schizophrenics.

correct_answers.text: The reduction in hippocampal volume in male schizophrenics was smaller than that in female schizophrenics.

questions.explanation: As compared to controls, in the schizophrenic group, the hippocampal formation was significantly smaller in the right as compared to the left hemisphere. The reduction in hippocampal volume in male schizophrenics was greater than that in females.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is incorrect with regards to the signalling that occurs at the synapse?

options.text: Chemical synapse is the commoner type, in which a chemical neurotransmitter is stored in the presynaptic vesicles.
Electrical synapse works much faster that the chemical synapse, due to the direct membrane to membrane connection via the gap junctions.
Excitatory postsynaptic potentials could occur in the postsynaptic membrane, following the release of an excitatory neurotransmitter.
Inhibitory postsynaptic potentials could occur following the release of an inhibitory neurotransmitter from the presynaptic neuron at the central inhibitory synapses.
One EPSP is usually sufficient to initiate an action potential.

correct_answer.text: One EPSP is usually sufficient to initiate an action potential.

correct_answers.text: One EPSP is usually sufficient to initiate an action potential.

questions.explanation: This is incorrect. Summation (temporal or spatial) can occur to allow the degree of depolarization to reach the critical threshold.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the structural changes seen on neuroimaging for patients with depression?

options.text: Reduction in the size of the frontal lobe, cerebellum and basal ganglia

questions.explanation: Asymmetry in temporal lobe is commonly observed in patients with bipolar disorder and not observed on neuroimaging in patients with depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: Varenicline could be used for tobacco withdrawal syndrome, which develops usually if a person stops smoking after 3–10 weeks of tobacco consumption. The mechanism of action of varenicline is that
questions.explanation: The tobacco withdrawal syndrome usually develops when a person stops smoking after 3–10 weeks of tobacco consumption. The onset may be within an hour after the last cigarette. The aforementioned medication has high affinity to the alpha-4 beta-2 nicotine Ach receptors and helps to prevent the withdrawal syndrome.

questions.question_text: Bupropion is one of the other alternative medications that has been indicated for the treatment of tobacco withdrawal syndrome. Which one of the following statements about it is incorrect?

options.text: It is actually an antidepressant with noradrenergic activity that reduces the effect of nicotine withdrawal.
The starting dose is usually 150 mg per day.
The most common side effect is insomnia.
The major side effect and risk is the development of epilepsy.
Contraindications to treatment would include a past history of epilepsy, eating disorders, CNS tumour and bipolar disorder.

correct_answer.text: The most common side effect is insomnia.

correct_answers.text: The most common side effect is insomnia.

questions.explanation: Based on existing research, the most common side effect is headache that occurs in around 30% of patients, followed closely by insomnia and then rash.

questions.question_text: Robertsonian translocations that occur in Down's syndrome usually involve chromosome 21 and which one of the following chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Robertsonian translocations are caused by the fusion of chromosome 14 and chromosome 21. The extra chromosome is usually of maternal origin and this happens in around 90% of the cases.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old female has a child diagnosed with Down's syndrome. She is concerned about having another child with Down's syndrome. Which one of the following maternal serum markers at 16 weeks of gestation is indicative of an increased likelihood of Down's syndrome?

options.text: Increased HCG, lowered alpha-fetoprotein, lowered unconjugated estriol
Increased HCG, increased alpha-fetoprotein, lowered unconjugated estriol

correct_answer.text: Increased HCG, lowered alpha-fetoprotein, lowered unconjugated estriol

correct_answers.text: Increased HCG, lowered alpha-fetoprotein, lowered unconjugated estriol

questions.explanation: The aforementioned combination of maternal serum markers present at 16 weeks is indicative of the likelihood of the development of Down's syndrome.

questions.question_text: In which of the following genetic conditions is the concept of anticipation best seen in?
questions.explanation: The concept of anticipation refers to the occurrence of an autonomic dominant disorder at earlier ages of onset and with greater severity in the succeeding generations. Huntington's disease is caused by the expansions of unstable triplet repeat sequences.

questions.question_text: Based on neuroanatomy, which one of the following marks the division between the frontal and the parietal lobe?
questions.explanation: The central sulcus marks the division between the frontal and the parietal lobes.

questions.question_text: In this particular form of amnesia, the clinical presentation is usually atypical and cannot be simply explained by ordinary forgetfulness. It is also commonly associated with 'la belle indifference' and has a highly unpredictable course. Which one of the following terminology best describes this particular form of amnesia?
questions.explanation: Psychogenic amnesia is part of the dissociative disorder consisting of a sudden inability to recall important personal data. The amnesia may be localized or generalized. The amnesia may be selective or continuous. It is true that the clinical presentation is usually atypical and cannot be explained by ordinary forgetfulness. Psychogenic amnesia is associated with la belle indifference (lack of concern) and a highly unpredictable course.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications should not be used in the treatment of an acute manic episode?
questions.explanation: The treatment of acute mania is usually with antipsychotics, such as (a) and (b). Lithium carbonate could be used in the prophylaxis, or could also be used in the treatment of acute mania episodes. Neuroleptics are usually preferred as the first-line drug of choice, though. Short-term benzodiazepines could also be used to help control behaviour difficulties or agitation. It is essential to ensure that medications such as antidepressants are stopped, as they could precipitate the manic episode.

questions.question_text: Based on the theories of genetic inheritance, male-to-male transmission is not possible for which of the following?
questions.explanation: For X-linked recessive disorder, male-to-male transmission would not take place. Males are far more likely to be affected with X-linked recessive disorder, and females are more likely to be carriers.

questions.question_text: Working through, enactment, containment of anxiety and resolution of conflicts are part of which modality of psychotherapy?
questions.explanation: These are part of brief dynamic therapy. In brief dynamic therapy, it is important to establish a therapeutic alliance, and then set goals and allow free association by the client. There is a need to focus on internal conflicts and interpretation of transference. Confrontation, working through and enactment can be used. Eventually, it is hoped that there will be resolution of conflicts and the client would be able to link the past, present and the transference.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about what Carl Jung has proposed as compared to Freud is incorrect?

options.text: Jung discounted libido being confined to being sexual, but considered libido as being the unitary force out of every manifestation of psychic energy.
Jung proposed the ideology of the collective unconscious.
Jung's theory consists of causality and teleology only.
Jung's theory views the contents of dreams within a framework in which archetypes may be projected onto others.
Five important type of archetypes are identified in his theory.

correct_answer.text: Jung's theory consists of causality and teleology only.

correct_answers.text: Jung's theory consists of causality and teleology only.

questions.explanation: His theory also includes synchronicity, which offers an explanation in terms of causation at the boundary of the physical world with the psychical world.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about mitochondrial inheritance is true?

options.text: Mitochondrial DNA is essentially maternally inherited.
There is the occurrence of anticipation amongst the generations.
Mitochondrial inheritance leads to the effect of genomic imprinting.
Mitochondrial inheritance leads to the effect of mosaicism.
Mitochondrial inheritance leads to the effect of uniparental disomy.

correct_answer.text: Mitochondrial DNA is essentially maternally inherited.

correct_answers.text: Mitochondrial DNA is essentially maternally inherited.

questions.explanation: The aforementioned is true. Mitochondrial inheritance may explain some cases of disorders that affect both males and females but that are transmitted through females and not through males.

questions.question_text: The posterior part of the superior temporal gyrus forms which one of the following structures?
questions.explanation: The posterior part of the superior temporal gyrus, area 22, forms on the left, the Wernicke's area. It has been noted that lesions involved with this particular area could lead to a resultant receptive aphasia.

questions.question_text: The neuroimaging scan showed that James has suffered an injury involving his dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Which of the following is not one of the residual symptoms that he might have?
questions.explanation: All of the aforementioned options are the residual symptoms caused by frontal lobe lesions, with the exception of alexia without agraphia. Alexia without agraphia occurs when there is an occlusion of the left posterior cerebral artery which leads to an infarction of the medial aspect of the left occipital lobe and the splenium of the corpus callosum.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes the mechanism of action of lofexidine, which is a substitute non-opiate usually given for opiate treatment?
questions.explanation: It acts primarily as an alpha-2 agonist, which acts centrally to reduce the sympathetic tone and hence will lead to a reduction in the blood pressure. The indication for use are for detoxification within a short period of time and for dependence in young people.

questions.question_text: Concordance between monozygotic twins in an autosomal dominant disorder has been estimated to be
questions.explanation: Autosomal dominant disorders result from the presence of an abnormal dominant allele, thus causing the individual to manifest the abnormal phenotypic trait. Males and females are affected, and male-to-male transmission can take place.

questions.question_text: Cognitive analytic therapy is a combination of cognitive and analytic therapy. Which of the following terminology correctly describes the extreme pessimism about the future, even before a plan is started?
questions.explanation: Snag refers to the extreme pessimism about the future, which would halt a plan before it even starts. Traps refer to the repetitive cycles of behaviour and their consequences become perpetuation. Dilemma refers to false choices or unduly narrowed options.

questions.question_text: Reframing and circular questioning are commonly used in which forms of the following therapies?
questions.explanation: Systemic family therapy uses the aforementioned techniques. Reframing occurs when an individual's problem is being framed as a family problem. Circular questioning is used to examine perspective of each family member on interfamily member relationship. Circular questioning aims at discovering and clarifying conflicting views. Hypothesis could be formed from conflicting views and the therapist can propose further changes.

questions.question_text: Research has found multiple genes to be associated with the onset of schizophrenia. In particular, the neuregulin gene has been implicated. On which of the following chromosome could the gene be located?
questions.explanation: The gene responsible is located on chromosome 8.

questions.question_text: Based on classification by size, which of the following is the largest neuron?
questions.explanation: Golgi type I would be the largest neuron due to it having a relatively long axon.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about action potential is incorrect?

options.text: During an action potential, the membrane potential rapidly becomes positive, before returning to become negative.
An action potential is propagated by the depolarization spreading laterally to adjacent parts of the neuron.
The passage of an action potential along a neuron is an all or none phenomenon.
The greater the diameter of the un-myelinated fibre, the slower the rate of conduction.
For conduction in myelinated fibres, the action potential appears to jump from one node of Ranvier to the next.

correct_answer.text: The greater the diameter of the un-myelinated fibre, the slower the rate of conduction.

correct_answers.text: The greater the diameter of the un-myelinated fibre, the slower the rate of conduction.

questions.explanation: This is incorrect. The greater the diameter of the fibre, the faster is the rate of transmission.

questions.question_text: A core trainee has been asked to assess James, who has suffered from an infarction involving the anterior cerebral artery. Which of the following psychiatric manifestations would be the most commonly seen for patients like James?
questions.explanation: An insult to the frontal lobe is likely to result in personality changes. It is important to note that left frontal lobe damage would result in non-fluent speech as well as depression. Involvement of the right frontal lobe would result in disinhibition and antisocial behaviour.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes the mechanism of action of ketamine, a commonly abused substance in the United Kingdom?

options.text: Competitive inhibition of the NMDA receptor complex
Inhibitory action on the GABA-A receptor
Blockage of the NMDA glutamate receptors

correct_answer.text: Competitive inhibition of the NMDA receptor complex

correct_answers.text: Competitive inhibition of the NMDA receptor complex

questions.explanation: Ketamine is considered to be the shorter-acting derivative of PCP. The action of ketamine is mediated via competitive inhibition from the NMDA receptor complex. Use of ketamine will lead to cramps, fatigue, depression and irritability. It may also lead to violent reactions such as flashbacks and harm to others.

questions.question_text: The catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) gene has been implicated in the causation of schizophrenia as well as bipolar disorder. On which one of the following chromosomes could the gene be located?
questions.explanation: The COMT gene that is responsible for the causation of both schizophrenia and bipolar disorder is located on chromosome 22.

questions.question_text: A child has chronic clinginess and ambivalence towards the mother. Which form of attachment type is this?
questions.explanation: In insecure attachment, there is chronic clinginess and ambivalence towards the mother. Clinically, this is very relevant, as it could lead to childhood emotional disorders (such as school refusal) as well as disorders in childhood and adulthood.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the objectives of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) when it is being used to treat individuals with depression?

options.text: Alleviation of symptoms by allowing the client to identify and challenge negative cognitions
Helping them to rehearse new cognitive responses towards difficult situations
Helping them to rehearse new behaviour responses towards difficult situations
Helping them to improve self-understanding by developing capacity for self-reflection

correct_answer.text: Helping them to improve self-understanding by developing capacity for self-reflection

correct_answers.text: Helping them to improve self-understanding by developing capacity for self-reflection

questions.explanation: The objectives of CBT for depression are as aforementioned, with the exception of (e). That is an objective of brief dynamic psychotherapy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about XYY syndrome is incorrect?

options.text: It tends to affect around 1 in 1000 male neonates.
An estimated 3% of patients in maximum security hospitals tend to have the XYY karyotype.
Individuals, especially females, with this genotype tend to have an increased rate of petty crime.
The mode of inheritance of this disorder is due to the primary nondisjunction of the Y chromosome.
Almost 10% of them have mosaic, which means that they have 46XY and 47 XYY chromosomes.

correct_answer.text: Individuals, especially females, with this genotype tend to have an increased rate of petty crime.

correct_answers.text: Individuals, especially females, with this genotype tend to have an increased rate of petty crime.

questions.explanation: It has been shown that males with this particular genotype tend to have an increased rate of petty crime instead. This could be a result of the resultant impulsiveness.

questions.question_text: Connecting pathways of the limbic systems include all of the following, with the exception of
questions.explanation: All of the aforementioned represent connecting pathways of the limbic system, with the exception of (e).

questions.question_text: Which of the following about the ultrastructural pathology of the deposits found in Alzheimer's dementia is correct?
questions.explanation: The plaques that are found contain mainly a core of amyloid. This consists of 8-nm extracellular filaments made up mainly of amyloid beta peptide. This has been derived from the membrane-bound beta amyloid precursor protein.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the CATIE (Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness) is incorrect?

options.text: The comparison drugs include olanzapine, quetiapine, risperidone, ziprasidone and perphenazine.
The sample size involved almost 150 subjects.
The trial demonstrated that the efficacy of first-generation antipsychotics was inferior to that of second-generation antipsychotics.
Olanzapine was considered to be the most effective in terms of the rates of discontinuation.
Olanzapine was associated with greater weight gain and an increase in the measure of glucose and lipid metabolism.

correct_answer.text: The trial demonstrated that the efficacy of first-generation antipsychotics was inferior to that of second-generation antipsychotics.

correct_answers.text: The trial demonstrated that the efficacy of first-generation antipsychotics was inferior to that of second-generation antipsychotics.

questions.explanation: The trial showed similar efficacy for first-generation and second-generation antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following terminologies correctly describes the process by which proteins are being generated from the original DNA template?
questions.explanation: It is known that following transcription, splicing and nuclear transport, translation is the process in gene expression whereby the mRNA acts as a template allowing the genetic code to be deciphered to allow the formation of a peptide chain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about psychological treatments for OCD is incorrect?

options.text: For initial treatment of OCD, exposure and response prevention (ERP) of up to 10 therapist hours per client is indicated.
For initial treatment of OCD, brief individual CBT using self-help materials and by telephone and group CBT should be offered.
For adults with OCD with mild-to-moderate functional impairment, more intensive CBT (including ERP) is recommended.
For children and young people with OCD with mild functional impairments, CBT and ERP are first-line treatments.
For children and young people with OCD with moderate-to-severe functional impairment, CBT and ERP are not the first line of treatment.

correct_answer.text: For children and young people with OCD with moderate-to-severe functional impairment, CBT and ERP are not the first line of treatment.

correct_answers.text: For children and young people with OCD with moderate-to-severe functional impairment, CBT and ERP are not the first line of treatment.

questions.explanation: CBT and ERP are indicated to be the first line of treatment for children and young people even if they have moderate-to-severe functional impairments.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychological therapies will be the most effective for an individual with excessive fears of contamination and recurrent compulsions of hand washing?
questions.explanation: Based on the NICE guidelines, exposure and response prevention (up to 10 therapist hours per client) is indicated for the initial treatment of OCD.

questions.question_text: Patients with the karyotype XXY would have all of the following clinical features, with the exception of

options.text: Better verbal skills as compared to performance skills
Aggression and antisocial traits in adulthood

correct_answer.text: Better verbal skills as compared to performance skills

correct_answers.text: Better verbal skills as compared to performance skills

questions.explanation: It has been noted that those with the aforementioned karyotype would have difficulties in acquiring verbal skills, along with a mild level of intellectual disability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants has the lowest approximate prevalence of sexual dysfunction?
questions.explanation: Among all the options, it has the lowest prevalence of sexual dysfunction, estimated to be at 25%. It does cause decreased libido and delayed orgasm. Erectile dysfunction and absence of orgasm are less common.

questions.question_text: The main types of neuroglia which are present in the CNS include all of the following, except
questions.explanation: These are the main types of neuroglia which are present in the peripheral nervous system instead of the central nervous system.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not affected by age?
questions.explanation: Option (b) is not influenced by age changes. Tasks that have been learnt over a lifetime relying on overlearned abilities are actually the most resistant to age-related changes. This is also known as crystallized intelligence. It is of importance to note that tasks that require the less practised processing of new information are most sensitive to age-related decline, or also known as fluid intelligence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about mania in patients who have suffered from cerebrovascular accident (CVA) is incorrect?

options.text: The incidence and prevalence of mania have been estimated to be around 0.5%–.1%.
CVA in the left hemisphere has a stronger association with mania.
Post-CVA mania is usually associated with cortical and subcortical lesions.
CVA in the thalamus is associated with mania.
Post-CVA mania usually occurs 3–9 months after stroke, and the first episode could either be mania or depression.

correct_answer.text: CVA in the left hemisphere has a stronger association with mania.

correct_answers.text: CVA in the left hemisphere has a stronger association with mania.

questions.explanation: It has been shown that CVA in the right hemisphere has a stronger association with mania in comparison to CVA in the left hemisphere.

questions.question_text: It has been known that variable expressivity could cause clinical features of autosomal dominant disorder to vary between affected individuals. Which terminology refers to whether a particular disorder would be manifested?
questions.explanation: Penetrance refers to the percentage of individuals who would express a particular phenotype. Variable expressivity, in association with penetrance might at times give the impression that a particular disorder has skipped a generation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following modality of psychological therapy has been demonstrated to be of some benefit for patients with post-myocardial infarction depression?
questions.explanation: Based on the ENRICHD (Enhancing Recovery in Coronary Heart Disease Study), there was noted to be substantial improvement in the severity of depression 6 months after the commencement of CBT. However, these beneficial effects have seemed to have diminished after 30 months.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about structural family therapy, as previously proposed, is incorrect?

options.text: Families are viewed as systems that operate through subsystems.
Each subsystem would require adequate boundaries.
Family problems tend to arise when the boundaries are too tight, thus resulting in enmeshment.
Structural family therapy identifies the set of unspoken rules governing the hierarchy, sharing of responsibilities and boundaries.
Therapist might present the identified rules to the family in a paradoxical way to bring about changes.

correct_answer.text: Family problems tend to arise when the boundaries are too tight, thus resulting in enmeshment.

correct_answers.text: Family problems tend to arise when the boundaries are too tight, thus resulting in enmeshment.

questions.explanation: When the boundaries are too tight, this would result in disengagement. When the boundaries are too loose, it will result in enmeshment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not considered to be an external indicator for family-based therapy?

options.text: Addition of members to the family
Knowledge that a family member has been recently diagnosed with a particular terminal illness
Change in financial status within the family
Change in marital status within the family

questions.explanation: Behaviour control problems are considered to be internal indicators for family-based therapy. When there are behaviour control problems within the family, it is pertinent to engage the family to deliver the behaviour therapy within the context of the home environment.

questions.question_text: A 12-year-old obese boy has a learning disability and was referred to the learning disability service. His parents commented that he seemed to have excessive hunger drive and he will resort to excessive skin picking at times. Which of the following conditions is he most likely to have?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation is characteristic for Prader–Willi syndrome. This is an autosomal dominant disorder that is commonly due to the deletion of chromosome of the paternal origin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is not considered to be established treatments for bipolar depression?
questions.explanation: The aforementioned options are considered to be established treatments for bipolar depression, with the exception of valproate. There is limited evidence of using valproate. It will probably protect against a depressive relapse but the current research database is small.

questions.question_text: What is the known mechanism of action of memantine?

options.text: Modulation of nicotine receptor via upregulation
Modulation of nicotine receptor via down-regulation
Uncompetitive antagonist at the NMDA receptor

correct_answer.text: Uncompetitive antagonist at the NMDA receptor

correct_answers.text: Uncompetitive antagonist at the NMDA receptor

questions.explanation: Memantine is a low-affinity voltage-dependent uncompetitive antagonist at the NMDA receptor. It might be neuro-protective and disease modifying.

questions.question_text: All of the following are known functions of astrocytes, with the exception of

options.text: Provision of structural support of neurons
Formation of the CNS neuroglial scar tissue

questions.explanation: CNS myelin sheath formation is a function of the oligo-dendrocytes and not a function of the astrocytes.

questions.question_text: The neurological condition of alexia without agraphia is usually caused by a lesion involving which areas of the cortex?
questions.explanation: This is usually due to an occlusion of the left posterior cerebral artery, which leads to infarction of the medial aspect of the left occipital lobe and the splenium of the corpus callosum.

questions.question_text: A lesion involving the left inferior frontal lobe as well as the insula would lead to which of the following type of apraxia?
questions.explanation: An insult to the left inferior frontal lobe and insula would lead to orobuccal apraxia. The patient will have difficulty in preforming learned, skilled movements of the face, lips, tongue, check, larynx and pharynx on command.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the CUTLASS (Cost Utility of the Latest Antipsychotic Drugs in Schizophrenia Study) is incorrect?

options.text: The study compared first-generation antipsychotics with second-generation antipsychotics.
The study included clozapine in the intervention.
The participants were randomly prescribed either first-generation antipsychotics or second-generation antipsychotics.
Patients in the first-generation antipsychotic arm showed a trend towards greater improvement in quality-of-life scale and symptom scales.
Overall, all the patients reported no clear preference for either first- or second-generation antipsychotics.

correct_answer.text: The study included clozapine in the intervention.

correct_answers.text: The study included clozapine in the intervention.

questions.explanation: (b) is incorrect. In the study, second-generation antipsychotics were included, but with the exception of clozapine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antipsychotics has the greatest propensity to raise prolactin?
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics decrease dopaminergic transmission, which in itself can decrease libido but may also increase prolactin levels via negative feedback. The overall propensity of an antipsychotic to cause sexual dysfunction is much similar to its propensity to raise prolactin: risperidone > haloperidol > olanzapine > quetiapine > aripiprazole.

questions.question_text: Based on current research, which one of the following proteins is the most significant risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's dementia?
questions.explanation: It is believed that late-onset AD is an autosomal dominant trait with age-dependent expression and low penetrance, resulting in apparent sporadic causes (to add explanation).

questions.question_text: Interpretation and confrontation are techniques commonly used in which one of the following psychological therapies?
questions.explanation: Interpretation of transference and confrontation, which is an attempt to make the client face the issues that are close to consciousness but are repressed or denied by the client, is an aspect of brief dynamic psychotherapy.

questions.question_text: Approximately what percentage of patients with anorexia nervosa will continue to have no improvement in their weight, menstrual pattern and eating behaviour and might even die from the condition?
questions.explanation: Approximately 20% of patients with anorexia nervosa will have poor outcome with no improvement and will eventually result in death.

questions.question_text: The presence of which of the following factors will help to reduce the risk of Alzheimer's dementia?

options.text: Previous known psychiatric history with previous treatment
Known vascular risk factors, but under treatment
Moderate level of physical activity (less than three times a week)

questions.explanation: Protective factors that would reduce the risk of development of Alzheimer's dementia include the following: bilingualism, cognitive engagement and late retirement, fish intake (more than once a week), high level of education (longer than 15 years), high level of physical activities (more than three times a week) and the use of NSAIDs and statin.

questions.question_text: A child has a relatively short stature, but with relatively mild learning disability. In addition, there are some subtle defects in visuospatial perception. Which of the following genetic deficits could this be due to?
questions.explanation: The clinical features are suggestive of Turner's syndrome. This is usually due to nondisjunction of the paternal XY that results in sexual chromosomal monosomy; 50% of the patients will have a karyotype consisting of 45XO or 46XX.

questions.question_text: A 6-year-old boy has the following clinical features: ventricular septal defect, hypocalcaemia and short stature. This is likely to be due to a microdeletion involving which one of the following chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The clinical features are congruent with DiGeorge syndrome. This involves a microdeletion in the chromosome 22q11.2.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old male has been on lithium monotherapy has the following symptoms: convulsions, syncope and oliguria. Which one of the following treatments should be considered immediately?
questions.explanation: He is having signs and symptoms of a severe overdose of lithium, with the expected lithium plasma level of more than 2mM. Immediate haemodialysis should be commenced.

questions.question_text: Based on the neuroanatomical findings, the cerebellum is derived from which one of the following primitive structures?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum is derived from the aforementioned structure. The oral part of the medulla oblongata as well as the cerebellum is also derived from the aforementioned structure.

questions.question_text: Nondominant temporal lobe damage would lead to significant impairments in terms of performance on this particular test
questions.explanation: This is a visual memory test in which the subject is presented with a complex design. The subject is asked to copy the design and then, 40 minutes later, without previous notification that this will occur, is then asked to draw the same design from memory. It is noted that nondominant temporal lobe damage will lead to impaired performance on this test. Dominant temporal lobe damage would lead to verbal memory difficulties.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the neurochemical 'acetylcholine' is incorrect?

options.text: It is synthesized from both acetyl-CoA and choline.
It is made usually in the cytoplasm of the cholinergic nerve terminals.
Choline is usually obtained from dietary sources.
The final step in the synthesis is usually catalysed by the enzyme choline acetyltransferase.
In Alzheimer's dementia, the activity of the enzyme is increased and this leads to a reduction in the synthesis of acetylcholine.

correct_answer.text: In Alzheimer's dementia, the activity of the enzyme is increased and this leads to a reduction in the synthesis of acetylcholine.

correct_answers.text: In Alzheimer's dementia, the activity of the enzyme is increased and this leads to a reduction in the synthesis of acetylcholine.

questions.explanation: This is incorrect. The activity of the enzyme is reduced, and hence there is a reduction in the synthesis of the acetylcholine.

questions.question_text: Pick's disease has an average age of onset of 45–65 years, with a female-to-male ratio of 2:1. Fifty per cent of patients who have this disorder are due to inheritance of which chromosome?
questions.explanation: 50% of patients with this disorder are caused by autosomal dominant inheritance of tau gene on chromosome 17. This will result in abnormal insoluble tau isoforms being accumulated in the neurons and also in the glia.

questions.question_text: Having a history of deliberate self-harm is a long-term predictor of suicide. Approximately what percentage of patients eventually kill themselves in the year following their deliberate self-harm?
questions.explanation: Approximately 1% of patients eventually kill themselves in the year following their deliberate self-harm.

questions.question_text: Based on the findings from the National Confidential Inquiry into Suicide, what is the estimated number of general population suicides that occur per year in England and Wales?
questions.explanation: The estimated number of general population suicides that occur per year in England and Wales has been estimated to be between 4500 and 5000.

questions.question_text: With regards to the genetic condition known as fragile X, individuals with full mutations usually have approximately how many repeats at the fragile X mental retardation gene?
questions.explanation: The normal number of repeats has been estimated to be 30. For carriers, they usually will have between 55 to 200 repeats. Full mutation usually involves having more than 200 repeats, which leads to hypermethylation at the gene.

questions.question_text: Paliperidone acts on which one of the following dopamine receptors?
questions.explanation: It has its action on the dopamine D2 receptors. All clinically effective antipsychotic drugs occupy a substantial proportion of the D2 receptors in the brain. This is usually between 70% and 80% at normal doses of the antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describe the mechanism of action of the common dementia medication known as rivastigmine?

options.text: It is a partial inhibitor of AChE.
It is a complete inhibitor of AChE.
It is an inhibitor of both AChE and BChE.
It is a partial inhibitor of BChE.
It is a complete inhibitor of BChE.

correct_answer.text: It is an inhibitor of both AChE and BChE.

correct_answers.text: It is an inhibitor of both AChE and BChE.

questions.explanation: AChEIs are largely broadly similar in their mechanism of action, and they are chosen usually based on their costs, their side effect profiles and patients' preferences. Rivastigmine is commonly used for AD as well as DLB and dementia related to Parkinson's disease. It inhibits both the enzymes. It does not modulate the nicotine receptor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a type of apraxia?
questions.explanation: Apraxia refers to an inability in performing purposive volitional acts, which does not result from paresis, incoordination, sensory loss or involuntary movements. Global apraxia is not one of the commonly known forms of apraxia.

questions.question_text: In this particular condition, an individual is unable to recognize the overall meaning of a picture, whereas the individual details are still being understood. Which terminology best describes the aforementioned?
questions.explanation: This is the correct terminology for the aforementioned deficits. This is usually associated with a lesion in the anterior part of the occipital lobe.

questions.question_text: Hypertensive crisis might result when food rich in tyramine is eaten when a patient has been started on MAO-I. Such a reaction will not happen when which one of the following is consumed?
questions.explanation: Cheese, with the exception of cottage cheese and cream cheese, does cause the typical reaction when consumed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants is indicated for the treatment of patients with post-myocardial infarction depression?
questions.explanation: Based on the Sertraline Antidepressant Heart Attack Randomized Trial (SADHART), the study has found that sertraline is a safe treatment for depression immediately after myocardial infarction. It is notable that the effects of sertraline were greater in the patients with severe and recurrent depression.

questions.question_text: Damage to which area of the brain will result in conduction dysphasia?
questions.explanation: Damage to the aforementioned region will result in conduction dysphasia in which the person is unable to repeat what is said by another. Of importance, comprehension and verbal fluency do remain intact.

questions.question_text: It is not uncommon that patients with Down's syndrome do present with early-onset cognitive impairment and even dementia. This is mediated by the action of which one of the following chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Individuals with Down's syndrome are at a high risk for developing Alzheimer's dementia. Over the age of 40, there is a high incidence of neurofibrillary tangles and plaques with an increase in P300 latency. This is largely due to a defect at 21q21.1 that leads to the overexpression of genes that encode for amyloid precursor protein.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a confounder that needs to be adjusted for when calculating either the standardized mortality rate or the standardized mortality ratio?
questions.explanation: The most important confounder that needs to be adjusted for is the age. The standardized mortality rate is the mortality rate adjusted to compensate for a confounder. The standardized mortality ratio is the ratio of the observed standardized mortality rate derived from the population being studied to the expected standardized mortality rate derived from a comparable standard population.

questions.question_text: Based on recent epidemiological studies, roughly what percentage of homicide perpetrators have a diagnosis of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: According to recent epidemiological studies, roughly 5% of homicide perpetrators have a diagnosis of schizophrenia. This percentage is much lower than the comorbidity of alcohol and drug misuse.

questions.question_text: Linkage studies have identified several genes to be responsible for the development of schizophrenia. The gene that affects synaptic plasticity and growth of neurons, which has also been implicated in the causation of schizophrenia, has been found to be located on which chromosome?
questions.explanation: The gene that is being referred to here is neuregulin and it is located on chromosome 8p12. It has been implicated in the aetiology of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: How does monamine oxidase help in the treatment of depression?

options.text: Via the inhibition of the reuptake of noradrenaline and serotonin
Increasing the availability of monoamines by inhibiting their metabolic degradation
Via the release of catecholamines from the neurons
Via the depletion of central monoaminergic neuronal stores of catecholamines

correct_answer.text: Increasing the availability of monoamines by inhibiting their metabolic degradation

correct_answers.text: Increasing the availability of monoamines by inhibiting their metabolic degradation

questions.explanation: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors increase the availability of monoamines by inhibiting their metabolic degradation by monoamine oxidase.

questions.question_text: Several neuroanatomical areas have been implicated in depression based on imaging findings. Which of the following associations is incorrect?

options.text: Amygdala: associated with memories of emotional reactions
Prefrontal cortex: associated with impairment in executive functions

questions.explanation: Based on neuroanatomy and imaging findings, the nucleus accumbens is associated with lack of motivation. The anterior cingulate cortex is associated with negative anticipation or poor judgement.

questions.question_text: PTSD patients tend to have a heightened physiological state after the traumatic event. This is due to the effects of which one of the following neurochemicals?
questions.explanation: The heightened physiological state specific to PTSD is mediated by noradrenergic and also the dopaminergic neurotransmitter systems, as well as the HPA axis.

questions.question_text: It has been known that antipsychotics such as risperidone have a higher affinity for the D2 receptors than for the D3 receptors. It is believed that approximately what percentage of the blockade of the D2 receptors is needed in order to achieve therapeutic response?
questions.explanation: It has been proven that approximately 75% blockade of the D2 receptors is required for there to be therapeutic response.

questions.question_text: Based on local epidemiological data, the highest number of post-discharge suicide cases occurred on which of the following day post-discharge?
questions.explanation: Post-discharge suicide is the most frequent in the first 2 weeks after leaving the hospital. The highest number usually occurred on the first day after leaving the hospital.

questions.question_text: Based on epidemiological studies, as compared to Afro-Caribbean probands, the risk of siblings of Caucasians to develop schizophrenia has been estimated to be around what percentage?
questions.explanation: In the UK, the risk of siblings of the Afro-Caribbean probands to develop schizophrenia has been estimated to be around 16%. In contrast, the risk of siblings of the Caucasian to develop schizophrenia has been estimated to be around 2%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following countries has been known to have the world's highest suicide rates?
questions.explanation: Lithuania, Estonia and Latvia are the countries that have been known to have the highest rate of suicide in the world.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the epidemiology of offending in the United Kingdom is incorrect?

options.text: The peak age of offending is around 14 years in girls.
The peak age of offending is around 15 years in boys.
Half of all the indictable crimes are committed by people under the age of 21 years.
By the age of 30 years, nearly 30% of all the males in the United Kingdom have been convicted of an indictable offense.

correct_answer.text: The peak age of offending is around 15 years in boys.

correct_answers.text: The peak age of offending is around 15 years in boys.

questions.explanation: All of the aforementioned statements are true, with the exception of (b). The peak age of offending is around 17–18 years in boys.

questions.question_text: Based on epidemiological studies, which of the following statements about depressive disorder is incorrect?

options.text: Prevalence in the general population is around 5%.
1 in 4 men and 1 in 10 women have been estimated to have depressive disorder in their lifetime.
The lifetime risk for first-degree relative is 20%.
In the United Kingdom, the lifetime prevalence of major depression with a seasonal pattern is 0.4%.
Male gender and older age are associated with seasonal pattern.

correct_answer.text: 1 in 4 men and 1 in 10 women have been estimated to have depressive disorder in their lifetime.

correct_answers.text: 1 in 4 men and 1 in 10 women have been estimated to have depressive disorder in their lifetime.

questions.explanation: Based on epidemiological studies, it has been estimated that one in four women and one in 10 men will have depressive disorder in their lifetime.

questions.question_text: All of the following are candidate genes that are associated with the development of schizophrenia, with the exception of
questions.explanation: It should be DTBNP1 (dystrobrevin-binding protein 1).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the sleep changes which occur in ageing is incorrect?

options.text: There is increased sleep latency or time to fall asleep.
There is increased frequency of awakenings at night.
There are increased episodes of fragmentation of REM sleep.
There is increased duration of slow-wave sleep.

correct_answer.text: There is increased duration of slow-wave sleep.

correct_answers.text: There is increased duration of slow-wave sleep.

questions.explanation: With ageing, there is decreased duration of slow-wave sleep, sleep efficacy as well as the total sleep time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the gender differences in schizophrenia is incorrect?

options.text: There is an approximate equal male-to-female ratio.
The mortality rate in men with schizophrenia is half that of women with schizophrenia.
Men with schizophrenia are most associated with more structural brain abnormalities.
Women tend to show a bimodal peak of incidence in their late 20s and 50s.

correct_answer.text: The mortality rate in men with schizophrenia is half that of women with schizophrenia.

correct_answers.text: The mortality rate in men with schizophrenia is half that of women with schizophrenia.

questions.explanation: Based on current literature, the mortality rate in men with schizophrenia has been estimated to be twice that of women with the similar condition.

questions.question_text: It has been known that antipsychotics may block the D2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway and this might result in the development of extra-pyramidal side effects (EPSE). EPSE usually emerges when approximately what percentage of the D2 receptors are blocked?
questions.explanation: EPSE emerge when around 80% of the D2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway are blocked.

questions.question_text: Based on local epidemiological data, what percentage of suicide occurs on the ward?
questions.explanation: 30% of suicide occurs on the ward, with the most common method being hanging.

questions.question_text: Approximately what percentage of patients with prodromal psychosis, which has developed into full-fledged schizophrenia, will achieve stable remission within 1 year?
questions.explanation: Approximately 80% of patients are able to achieve stable remission within 1 year.

questions.question_text: For those with prodromal symptoms suggestive of psychosis, the conversation rate to schizophrenia has been estimated to be around
questions.explanation: The conversion rate to schizophrenia has been estimated to be around 35% for those who are prodromal.

questions.question_text: Damage to which area of the brain will result in expressive dysphasia?
questions.explanation: Damage to the Broca's area will result in the loss of rhythm, intonation and grammatical aspects of speech. Comprehension is still normal, and the patient is aware that his or her speech is difficult for others to follow, thus resulting in marked distress and frustration.

questions.question_text: A therapist decides that it will be ideal for a patient who has been diagnosed with agoraphobia to have repeated exposure to crowd. This is based on which one of the following basic psychological concepts?
questions.explanation: This is based on the concept of extinction. Extinction refers to the gradual disappearance of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus has been repeatedly presented without the unconditioned stimulus.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old female came to the outpatient clinic and requested to stop her therapy sessions. She mentioned that the therapist was critical, which reminded of how her father used to treat her. This experience is termed as
questions.explanation: This is an example of transference. Transference is an unconscious process in which the patient transfers to the therapist feelings, emotions and attitudes that were experienced previously.

questions.question_text: Based on previous research findings, which one of the following is not a psychosocial factor that will predispose an individual towards developing PTSD?

options.text: Previous psychiatric history of antisocial behaviour

questions.explanation: Based on previous research, all of the aforementioned are predisposing psychosocial factors. However, females tend to be more affected than males.

questions.question_text: Based on epidemiological studies, which of the following is true with regards to the percentage of individuals in the community who have severe learning disabilities?
questions.explanation: The definition for severe mental retardation will include those whose IQ range is between 20 and 34. This affects around 3% of those who have learning disability.

questions.question_text: A lesion in the arcuate fasciculus would result in impairments in the following, with the exception of
questions.explanation: It is the region of the brain that is responsible for transmission of information between the Wernicke's area and the Broca's area. A lesion involving that area would cause repetition to be impaired, but with preserved functioning in terms of fluency, comprehension and naming.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the epidemiology of substance misuse is incorrect?

options.text: For adolescents and young adults in the United Kingdom, approximately 50% have taken illicit drugs at some point in time.
Around 20% have used illicit drugs in the previous month.
The peak age of substance misuse is 15 years.
The male-to-female ratio has been estimated to be 3:1.
For opiate misuse, the mortality is increased by 12 times and the suicide rate is increased by 10 times.

correct_answer.text: The peak age of substance misuse is 15 years.

correct_answers.text: The peak age of substance misuse is 15 years.

questions.explanation: The peak age of substance misuse is 15 years based on existing epidemiological studies.

questions.question_text: According to the model proposed by Brown and Harris in 1978, which of the following psychosocial factors will not predispose an individual towards depression?

options.text: Having children who are younger than the age of 11

questions.explanation: Bereavement is not one of the predisposing factors that would predispose an individual to depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: Habit reversal is a useful psychological intervention for which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Habit reversal is an effective technique for Tourette's syndrome. It involves performing simultaneous incompatible movements to reduce the unwanted movements.

questions.question_text: A damage to which area of the brain will result in receptive dysphasia?
questions.explanation: It is important to note that damage to the Wernicke's area would disrupt the ability to comprehend language, either written or spoken. The patient also is unaware that his or her dysphasic speech is difficult for others to comprehend.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the epidemiology of insomnia is incorrect?

options.text: The estimated prevalence of the disorder is between 1% and 10% in the general population.
The estimated 1-year prevalence for adults could range to as high as 60%.
Prevalence is especially higher in the elderly population.
It has been estimated to affect around one fourth of the elderly population.
There is a predisposition for females to have the disorder as compared to males.

correct_answer.text: The estimated 1-year prevalence for adults could range to as high as 60%.

correct_answers.text: The estimated 1-year prevalence for adults could range to as high as 60%.

questions.explanation: The estimated 1-year prevalence in adults usually range between 15 and 40%.

questions.question_text: Based on existing epidemiological studies, what has been estimated to be the prevalence of schizophrenia amongst those with learning disabilities?
questions.explanation: The prevalence of people with learning disabilities who also have schizophrenia has been estimated to be around 3%. This is much higher than the average prevalence in the general population. It has been noted that the prevalence of schizophrenia is inversely related to the intelligence quotient (IQ). More importantly, a diagnosis of schizophrenia cannot be made if the IQ is considered to be less than 45.

questions.question_text: A 60-year-old male has recently suffered from a cerebrovascular event. Ever since the incident, he is unable to copy shapes or to discriminate between two versions of the same objects. This is most likely due to a lesion involving the
questions.explanation: It is essential to note that visuospatial elements are being perceived together into complete perceptions in the right parietal lobe. A lesion at the level of the right parietal lobe would result in apperceptive agnosia. Hence, the individual would not be able to copy shapes or discriminate between two versions of the same objects. In addition, he is not able to name the object when he or she sees it or touches it.

questions.question_text: The autopsy report of a man who died of Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease shows spongiform change in his brain. Which of the following pathological findings is associated with the spongiform change?

options.text: Amyloid beta deposition in entorhinal cortex
Hirano bodies in hippocampal pyramidal cells

questions.explanation: Microscopy of the brain materials reveals vacuolar changes in the grey matter particularly in cerebral and cerebellar cortex, creating characteristic spongiform changes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following genes is associated with Pick's disease?

options.text: Amyloid precursor protein gene on chromosome 21

questions.explanation: 50% of cases are caused by autosomal dominant inheritance of the tau gene on chromosome 17. This results in abnormal insoluble tau isoforms which accumulate in the neurons and the glia.

questions.question_text: A 60-year-old man suffers from mild cognitive impairment and his son wants to find out the rate of conversion into dementia every year. Your answer is
questions.explanation: The conversion rate to dementia has been estimated to be around 10% per year.

questions.question_text: Buprenorphine acts as a partial agonist at which of the following receptors?
questions.explanation: It is known to be a partial mu opioid agonist.

questions.question_text: Deletion in which of the following genes is associated with ubiquitin-positive and tau-negative frontotemporal dementia (FTD)?

options.text: Latent-transforming growth factor beta-binding protein gene

questions.explanation: Progranulin is a growth factor protein and its genetic locus deletion is associated with frontotemporal dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes confounding bias?

options.text: This bias occurs in clinical trials when treatment is chosen by personnel involved without randomization.
This bias occurs when comparisons are made between groups of participants that differ with respect to determinants of outcome other than those under study.
This bias occurs when the methods of measurements are consistently dissimilar among groups of participants.
This bias occurs when participants in one group are more likely to remember past events than participants in another study group.
This bias occurs when studies based on the prevalence produce very different results when compared with studies based on incidence of a disease.

correct_answer.text: This bias occurs when comparisons are made between groups of participants that differ with respect to determinants of outcome other than those under study.

correct_answers.text: This bias occurs when comparisons are made between groups of participants that differ with respect to determinants of outcome other than those under study.

questions.explanation: Option (a) refers to selection bias. Option (c) refers to measurement bias. Option (d) refers to recall bias. Option (e) refers to Neyman bias.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman suffers from depression and has taken tranylcypromine for 2 years. She presents to the Accident and Emergency Department with a blood pressure of 220/120 mmHg. A few hours ago, she went for a buffet dinner and consumed a large amount of mature cheese, red wine and smoked salmon. The Accident and Emergency Department consultant wants to find out from you the best medication to reduce her blood pressure. Your answer is
questions.explanation: This lady suffers from hypertensive crisis owing to consumption of food containing high levels of tyramine.

questions.question_text: A 4-year-old child is referred to you with delayed speech and language. He was initially suspected to suffer from autism. He has gaze aversion and social avoidance. His IQ is 60. He also has attention deficit. Physical examination shows enlarged testes, large ears, a long face and flat feet. Mental state examination reveals limited eye contact, perseveration of words, echolalia and hand flapping. The genetic mutation responsible for this disorder is
questions.explanation: This child suffers from fragile X syndrome.

questions.question_text: A 75-year-old man seems to develop Alzheimer's disease. His daughter has read an article stating that a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan can establish the diagnosis of early Alzheimer's disease. Which of the following MRI findings is associated with the diagnosis of early Alzheimer's disease?
Rivastigmine is a
questions.explanation: Option (d) refers to tacrine. Option (a) refers to donepezil and galantamine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following risk factors causes the late onset (ages 12–14 years) of delinquent behaviour in males?
questions.explanation: Options (b) to (e) are risk factors for early-onset (ages 6–11 years) delinquent behaviour.

questions.question_text: Name two symptoms associated with poor response to SSRIs. (Choose two options.)
Name two symptoms associated with poor response to CBT. (Choose two options.)
Name the most common obsession. (Choose one option.)
Name the most common compulsion. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: The most common obsessions (in descending order) are fear of contamination, doubting, fear of illness, germs or bodily fear, symmetry and sexual or aggressive thoughts. The most common compulsions are checking, washing and counting.

questions.question_text: The nurse asks the client if she can go through her things to ensure there are not any sharp objects that she could use to self-harm. The client becomes upset and feels like punching the nurse. Later when the client sees a psychotherapist she realizes that her desire to hit the nurse was related to her mother hitting her as a child. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Acting out is enacting an unconscious wish or fantasy impulsively as a way of avoiding painful affect.

questions.question_text: The client told the core trainee that she has thoughts of harming her partner and she has to tap on a table five times in order to dispel these thoughts. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Undoing is an attempt to negate sexual, aggressive or shameful implications from a previous comment or behaviour by elaborating, clarifying or doing the opposite.

questions.question_text: The core trainee inquires about her alcohol dependence, and the client informs her that she is not dependent on alcohol and that drinking is a way to ease the stress in her life. She feels that her drinking was within reason and gave an explanation for this. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Rationalization refers to the justification of unacceptable attitudes, beliefs or behaviours and making them tolerable to oneself.

questions.question_text: After speaking to the core trainee, she believes that the trainee is the best doctor whom she has ever seen. From now on, the patient only wants to see this core trainee as her doctor. (Choose two options.)
questions.explanation: Idealization refers to the attribution of perfect or near-perfect qualities to others as a way of avoiding anxiety or negative feelings. Splitting is compartmentalizing experiences of self and others such that integration is not possible.

questions.question_text: The core trainee asks you to give some examples of primitive defence. (Choose seven options.)
questions.explanation: Melanie Klein described projection and splitting but not denial.

questions.question_text: On the second day, the client worries that the consultant may give her a warning for hitting the nurse and behaving like a child on the ward. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Regression refers to an earlier phase or functioning to avoid the conflicts and tensions associated with current situation.

questions.question_text: Her behaviour became uncontrollable and she almost set fire to part of the ward. The consultant has decided to send her to a secure hospital. She complains that no one cares about her. She was chased away by her parents and now by the consultant. This verifies her belief that hospital staff are as abusive as her parents. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Projective identification has two phases: (1) the client first projected an internal object (i.e. uncaring parents in this case) to the consultant; (2) then, pressure is placed on the consultant to take on characteristics of the uncaring parents.

questions.question_text: The GP mentioned in his referral letter that the client has tried to separate himself from his emotions since his father died. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Isolation of affect refers to the separation of an idea from its associated affect to avoid emotional turmoil.

questions.question_text: During the interview, the client tells you that he has tried to block and expel grief from entering his mind. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Suppression refers to conscious effort not to attend to the certain state, feeling or impulse. On the other hand, repression refers to blockage or expulsion of unacceptable ideas or impulses in the inner states from entering the consciousness.

questions.question_text: During the interviewing, the client refers to abstract philosophy to explain his current state. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Intellectualization refers to the excessive use of abstract ideation to avoid difficult feelings.

questions.question_text: One month later, the client appears to take on the quality of his father by behaving like him. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Identification refers to internalization of the qualities of another person by behaving like that person.

questions.question_text: Two months later, the client informs you that he has internalized the hostility of his father to scold other staff in the business, as he feels sad for his father's sudden death. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Introjection means internalizing aspects of a significant person as a way of dealing with the loss of that person.

questions.question_text: You speak to his mother who expresses sympathy to doctors, as they are always busy and medical errors seem to be inevitable. She wants to apologize to the doctors who looked after her husband, as she was rude to him. Two weeks later, the client informs you that his mother is proceeding with the legal case and hopes to get a huge amount of compensation from the hospital. What is the defence mechanism used by his mother? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Reaction formation refers to the transformation of an unacceptable wish or impulse into its opposite.

questions.question_text: A 52-year-old has been admitted to the neurology unit. On clinical examination, he has optic ataxia, simultanagnosia and ocular apraxia.
questions.explanation: The clinical features are representative of the Balint's syndrome. This is usually due to lesions of the dorsal region and the adjoining parietal regions.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old male has been having contralateral hemiachromatopsia and dyslexia.
questions.explanation: Lesions of the left ventral region (inferior to the calcarine fissure) could lead to contralateral (right) acquired (central) hemiachromatopsia and acquired dyslexia.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old male presents to the emergency department with new-onset asteropsis and impaired visual motion perception.
questions.explanation: A bilateral occipital dorsal lesion could lead to the aforementioned clinical features.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old female presents to the emergency department with new-onset apperceptive visual agnosia.
questions.explanation: Lesions of the right ventral region could lead to contralateral (left) acquired hemiachromatopsia and apperceptive visual agnosia.

questions.question_text: This is a peptic hormone that is involved in the stimulation of the hepatic secretion of insulin-like growth factor 1.
questions.explanation: GH is a peptide hormone that stimulates the hepatic secretion of IGF-1. In turn, binding of IGF-1 to widespread IGF-binding proteins leads to stimulation of anabolism.

questions.question_text: This is a single-chain peptide that has an action on lactation.
questions.explanation: Prolactin is a single-chain peptide hormone that acts on the mammary glands to stimulate the secretion of milk (normally during lactation). It also inhibits the activity of the testes and the ovaries.

questions.question_text: In males, this hormone stimulates the seminiferous tubule Sertoli cells to promote the growth of spermatozoa.
questions.explanation: This hormone, in males, also stimulates the release of inhibin A and inhibin B.

questions.question_text: This hormone consists of two peptide chains, and the alpha chain is similar to that of FSH.
questions.explanation: LH consists of two peptide chains; the alpha chain is the same as that of the FSH. LH also stimulates the gonads (ovaries and testes).

questions.question_text: This hormone has a natriuretic action for both males and females.
questions.explanation: This hormone is a nonapeptide that stimulates the contraction of the uterine myometrium during parturition. In addition, it also stimulates the ejection of milk from the mammary glands during lactation.

questions.question_text: The usage of anxiolytics would cause which TWO of the changes on the EEG?
questions.explanation: They tend to cause an increase in the beta activity and a corresponding decrease in the alpha activity (sometimes).

questions.question_text: The usage of antidepressant would cause which ONE of the changes on the EEG?
questions.explanation: Antidepressants tend to cause an increase in delta activity.

questions.question_text: The usage of antipsychotic drugs would cause which TWO of the following changes on the EEG?
questions.explanation: Antipsychotic drugs could cause a decrease in beta activity as well as an increased in low-frequency delta activity and/or theta activity.

questions.question_text: Select four options that are characteristic for non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
questions.explanation: The characteristic features of NREM sleep include decreased recall of dreaming, decreased complexity of dreams, increased parasympathetic tone, upward ocular deviation with few or no movements, abolition of tendon reflexes, decreased heart rate, decreased systolic blood pressure, decreased respiratory rate and decreased cerebral blood flow. The penis is not usually erect as well.

questions.question_text: Select three options that are characteristic of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep.
questions.explanation: The characteristic features include increased recall of dreaming, increased complexity of dreams, increased sympathetic activity, transient runs of conjugate ocular movements, maximal loss of muscle tone, increased heart rate, increased systolic blood pressure, increased respiratory rate and increased cerebral blood flow. There will also be penile erection or increased vaginal blood flow. In rat brains, increased protein synthesis is noted.

questions.question_text: Select TWO of the aforementioned changes that are common in schizophrenia.
questions.explanation: In schizophrenia, there is a reduction in the dopamine in the mesocortical pathway and this causes anergy and loss of drive (predominantly the negative symptoms). The dopamine hypothesis proposes that increased levels of DA or DA receptors could cause schizophrenia. Galactorrhoea is seen in antipsychotic treatment as a result of the blockade of DA receptors.

questions.question_text: Select ONE of the aforementioned changes that is common for OCD.
questions.explanation: In this condition (OCD), there is noted to be an increase in dopamine in the nigrostriatal pathway. This is, in turn, responsible for the development of compulsive behaviour.

questions.question_text: Select TWO of the aforementioned changes that are common for bipolar disorder.
questions.explanation: The increased dopamine would cause an increased in sensory stimuli and movement. There is also, in turn, an increase in the CSF HVA levels in manic patients.

questions.question_text: This chromosome is implicated in DiGeorge syndrome.
questions.explanation: Chromosome 22 is associated with DiGeorge syndrome. In addition, it also codes for the COMT gene, which is implicated in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: This chromosome has been associated with autism.
questions.explanation: Chromosome 2q and Chromosome 7 have been implicated in autism.

questions.question_text: Patau's syndrome is due to abnormalities with this particular chromosome.
questions.explanation: There has been an association between Wilson's disease and this particular chromosome as well.

questions.question_text: Both of these genetic conditions (Angelman's and Prader–Willi) are due to abnormalities on this chromosome.
questions.explanation: Angelman's syndrome is due to a maternal chromosome 15 microdeletion, whereas Prader–Willi syndrome is due to a paternal chromosome 15 microdeletion.

questions.question_text: Which of the chromosomes has been implicated in inherited CJD?
questions.explanation: Chromosome 20 has been implicated in inherited CJD.

questions.question_text: This could potentially give rise to either silent or missense mutations.
questions.explanation: Substitution mutations could result in silent, missense or nonsense mutations.

questions.question_text: This refers to a mutation that causes a change from a purine to a pyrimidine.
questions.explanation: A transversion mutation causes a change from a purine to a pyrimidine or a pyrimidine to a purine.

questions.question_text: In this form of mutation, the mutation involves a change from a purine to a purine base.
questions.explanation: In a transition mutation, the change is usually from a purine to a purine or a pyrimidine to a pyrimidine.

questions.question_text: This results in the creation of a stop codon.
questions.explanation: A nonsense mutation would result in the creation of a stop codon, thus resulting in the premature termination of a protein that is being synthesized.

questions.question_text: This particular type of mutation results in a change in a reading frame, which might cause a loss-of-function mutation.
questions.explanation: If the number of nucleotides deleted or inserted in an exon involves multiples of three, then the sequence of codons or the reading frame is preserved. If it does not, the reading frame will be disrupted and this would result in a frameshift mutation with a truncated protein product.

questions.question_text: Presence of behavioural control problems within the family
questions.explanation: Behavioural control problems such as conduct disorder in a child are an internal indication for family-based therapy. Family therapy helps to engage the family to deliver behaviour therapy in a home environment.

questions.question_text: The common indications for this particular form of psychotherapy include dysthymia, depressive disorder and, in particular, bulimia nervosa.
questions.explanation: Research has indicated that interpersonal therapy for depressive disorder is equally effective as CBT. In addition, it is also indicated for eating disorder such as bulimia nervosa. Dysthymia disorder is another indication. Other issues that would render such a therapy useful include interpersonal disputes, role transition, grief as well as dealing with loss.

questions.question_text: This particular form of therapy is suitable for borderline personality disorders. The core conceptualization of this form of therapy is that individuals are unable to interpret their actions or others' actions.
questions.explanation: Mentalization refers to psychological minded and empathy. It is developed in people who have responsive parents providing secure attachment in childhood. Patients with BPD have impaired mentalization. As a result, they are not able to interpret their actions or others' actions based on intentional mental states such as beliefs, feelings and preferences. Impaired mentalization is associated with affect dysregulation and incoherent sense of self.

questions.question_text: This particular form of therapy involves dealing with faculty procedures such as traps, dilemma and snag.
questions.explanation: Traps refers to repetitive cycles of behaviour and their consequences that become perpetuation. Dilemma refers to false choices or unduly narrowed options. Snag refers to extreme pessimism about the future and halts a plan before it even starts.

questions.question_text: One part of this form of therapy is based on Mowrer's two-factor model.
questions.explanation: The theory states that the fear of a specific stimulus is acquired through classical conditioning and the client tries to reduce fear by avoiding the conditioned stimulus through operant conditioning. The cognitive component is based on Beck's cognitive model of depression that includes the effect of early experiences, core beliefs, underlying assumptions, cognitive distortions, automatic thoughts and the negative cognitive triad.

questions.question_text: Some of the possible negative reactions during this process of psychological therapy include resistance, acting-out, acting-in and negative therapeutic reaction.
questions.explanation: In resistance, the client is ambivalent about getting help and may even oppose attempts from the therapist who offers help. Resistance may manifest in the form of silence, avoidance or absences. In acting out, it refers to the poor containment of strong feelings triggered by the therapy. In acting in, it refers to the exploration of the therapist's personal and private information by the client or presenting a symbolic gift to the therapist. Negative therapeutic reaction refers to the sudden and unexpected deterioration or regression in apparent progression during therapy.
